label: LC-39B — SLS Launch Pad
sub: Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center is the primary launch pad for the Artemis program, rebuilt from Apollo/Shuttle-era infrastructure. All Artemis SLS/Orion missions launch from this pad.

label: Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB)
sub: The iconic VAB at KSC is where SLS and Orion are stacked and integrated before rollout to the launch pad. At 160 meters tall, it remains one of the largest buildings in the world by volume.

label: LC-36 — Blue Origin New Glenn
sub: Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is the dedicated launch pad for Blue Origin's New Glenn heavy-lift rocket, which first flew January 16, 2025. INCIDENT: On May 29, 2026, New Glenn exploded during a prelaunch static fire test, destroying the rocket and damaging LC-36. ROOT CAUSE (Aug 6, 2026): Blue Origin traced the explosion to a main oxygen valve issue on a BE-4 first-stage engine; modified valve hardware is due by end of August 2026. Blue Moon Mark 1's debut cargo lunar landing — needed for Moon Base I rover delivery — has slipped from late summer 2026 to Q1 2027 at the earliest, pending New Glenn's return to flight before year-end 2026.

label: Johnson Space Center (JSC)
sub: JSC in Houston serves as Mission Control for all Artemis crewed flights and is the home of NASA's Astronaut Corps. The Space Vehicle Mockup Facility (SVMF) at JSC now houses Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mk2 engineering mockup (delivered May 11, 2026) for Artemis IV crew training. The Artemis II crew — Wiseman, Glover, Koch, and Hansen — continue reconditioning here post-splashdown.

label: Goddard Space Flight Center
sub: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, MD manages Artemis-era science instruments and the Deep Space Network coordination. Goddard also oversees key Orion communications systems. On Aug 11, 2026, Goddard completed the Lunar Environment Monitoring Station (LEMS) seismometer payload, the first fully finished astronaut-deployed science instrument for the lunar surface, now awaiting assignment to an Artemis mission.

label: Marshall Space Flight Center
sub: NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, AL is the lead center for SLS development. Currently (May 2026): (1) Fabricating the Artemis III structural spacer — barrel section material is being machined, upper and lower rings are in work, with welding operations scheduled next — replacing the ICPS for the LEO rendezvous test mission targeting late 2027. (2) The Artemis II Orion heat shield will arrive at Marshall this summer for formal X-ray scans, ~2,000 CFD simulation validation, and Avcoat sample extractions that will define Artemis IV crewed landing readiness. Marshall also oversees the RS-25 engine procurement contract with Aerojet Rocketdyne.

label: Stennis Space Center
sub: NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi hosts the B-2 test stand where SLS underwent the Green Run engine tests in January and March 2021. Stennis is the primary facility for large rocket propulsion testing. AGREEMENT: On July 24, 2026, NASA and Blue Origin agreed to conduct New Glenn second-stage hot fire testing on the B-2 stand, targeted to begin fall 2026, supporting Blue Moon lunar lander missions for Artemis.

label: Michoud Assembly Facility (Boeing SLS)
sub: NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans is where Boeing manufactures the SLS core stage. The facility has manufactured rocket components since the Saturn V era. SLS core stages are built and shipped to Stennis for testing, then to KSC.

label: Lockheed Martin — Orion Prime (Colorado)
sub: Lockheed Martin's facility at Waterton Canyon, Colorado is the prime contractor headquarters for the Orion crew module. Final assembly and systems integration are performed at KSC, but Lockheed Martin leads all design, manufacturing, and testing.

label: Aerojet Rocketdyne — RS-25 Engines (Sacramento)
sub: Aerojet Rocketdyne's facility in Sacramento, CA manufactures and tests the RS-25 engines that power the SLS core stage. Sixteen heritage RS-25 engines from the Space Shuttle program were refurbished for Artemis I–IV; new production engines are being manufactured for subsequent flights.

label: Northrop Grumman — Gateway HALO (Redondo Beach)
sub: Northrop Grumman's facility in Redondo Beach, CA is building the Gateway HALO (Habitation and Logistics Outpost) module under an $935 million contract. Northrop Grumman also builds SLS solid rocket boosters with facilities in Utah and Florida.

label: SpaceX Headquarters (Hawthorne, CA)
sub: SpaceX's headquarters in Hawthorne, CA is where Starship HLS engineering and mission planning are coordinated. SpaceX holds the primary HLS contract ($2.89B) for Artemis III and beyond, developing a crewed lunar-capable Starship variant.

label: Starbase — SpaceX Starship (Boca Chica)
sub: SpaceX Starbase in Boca Chica, TX is the development and launch site for Starship/Super Heavy, the vehicle selected as the Artemis Human Landing System. IFT-12 (May 22, 2026) was the inaugural launch from Orbital Launch Pad 2 (OLP-2) — the first flight of Starship V3 (Block 3, Booster 19 + Ship 39). Ship 39 splashed down nominally in the Indian Ocean; Booster 19 was lost after a boostback burn anomaly. FAA mishap investigation underway. Ship 39 carried NASA-required docking port and propellant-transfer hardware, a structural milestone for Artemis III HLS qualification.

label: Blue Origin HQ — Blue Moon HLS (Kent, WA)
sub: Blue Origin's headquarters and primary manufacturing facility in Kent, WA is developing the Blue Moon Mk.2 crewed lunar lander under a $3.4B NASA contract. New Shepard and New Glenn propulsion and vehicle systems are also developed here.

label: ULA — Centaur V Manufacturing (Decatur, AL)
sub: United Launch Alliance's manufacturing facility in Decatur, AL produces Centaur upper stages. Following NASA's February 2026 cancellation of the SLS Exploration Upper Stage, ULA's Centaur V was selected as the new SLS upper stage for future missions.

label: Maxar Technologies — Gateway PPE (Palo Alto, CA)
sub: Maxar Technologies' facility in Palo Alto, CA is developing the Gateway Power and Propulsion Element (PPE), which will provide electrical power and high-power electric propulsion for the Lunar Gateway station using solar electric propulsion.

label: NASA Ames — Orion Heat Shield Testing
sub: NASA Ames Research Center in Silicon Valley conducted the 121-test heat shield investigation campaign following Artemis I's unexpected charring of the Avcoat material. The Arc Jet Complex at Ames simulated the extreme reentry heating conditions to diagnose the anomaly.

label: White Sands Test Facility — Orion Abort System Tests
sub: NASA's White Sands Test Facility in New Mexico is used for Orion launch abort system testing and propulsion system qualification. The Abort Motor and Attitude Control Motor for Orion's Launch Abort System were tested here prior to Artemis I.

label: Plum Brook Station — Orion Thermal Vacuum Testing
sub: NASA Glenn Research Center's Plum Brook Station in Sandusky, OH houses the Space Power Facility — the world's largest thermal vacuum chamber — where the Orion crew module and service module underwent combined environmental testing in 2019–2020 prior to Artemis I.

label: Axiom Space — Artemis Lunar Spacesuits (Houston)
sub: Axiom Space in Houston is the sole remaining contractor for next-generation Artemis lunar spacesuits (xEMU replacement), after Collins Aerospace discontinued its competing xEVAS development. Axiom's Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) will be used for Artemis III+ lunar surface operations.

label: Pacific Splashdown Zone — Orion Recovery
sub: The primary recovery zone for Orion capsules is in the Pacific Ocean west of Baja California. Artemis I splashed down here on December 11, 2022, recovered by the USS Portland. USS San Diego is designated as the primary recovery ship for Artemis II.

label: Northrop Grumman — SRB Testing (Promontory, UT)
sub: Northrop Grumman's Promontory, Utah facility manufactures and tests the five-segment solid rocket boosters used on SLS Block 1. Each SLS flight uses two SRBs derived from Space Shuttle technology, producing 3.6 million pounds of thrust combined. SHIPMENT: On June 2, 2026, the final 8 five-segment SRB motor segments for Artemis III departed the adjacent Northrop Grumman Railyard Shipping Facility in Corinne, UT, by Union Pacific rail for Kennedy Space Center — summer stacking now underway.

label: Canadian Space Agency HQ (Saint-Hubert, QC)
sub: The Canadian Space Agency headquarters in Saint-Hubert, Quebec is the home of Canada's astronaut office and Canadarm3 development program. Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — the first non-American on a lunar trajectory (Artemis II, April 2026) — is based here. The crew visited CSA HQ on May 14, 2026 for a bilingual public virtual event. Canada's crew seat on Artemis was earned through the Canadarm3 contribution; partnership terms are being renegotiated following Gateway's cancellation in March 2026.

label: Firefly Aerospace — MoonFall Drones (Cedar Park, TX)
sub: Firefly Aerospace's headquarters in Cedar Park, Texas, received a NASA Moon Base contract (announced May 26, 2026) for MoonFall hopping reconnaissance drones, to be deployed from the Elytra Dark spacecraft in a 50 km lunar orbit. The drones will survey the lunar south pole for site selection and support surface operations for the Moon Base program. Firefly also has a manufacturing and test facility near Briggs, TX.

label: Lunar Outpost — Pegasus LTV (Golden, CO)
sub: Lunar Outpost's headquarters in Golden, Colorado, received a $220 million NASA Moon Base contract (announced May 26, 2026) for the Pegasus Lunar Terrain Vehicle (LTV). The Pegasus LTV is capable of 9+ mph with autonomous, teleoperated, and crewed modes — competing against Astrolab's CLV-1 as NASA's second contracted crewed lunar terrain vehicle. Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance cargo lander will deliver both the Pegasus and CLV-1 rovers to the lunar south pole as part of Moon Base I (targeting fall 2026).
